scope: Aydinid-Menteshe eastern and southern frontier: Sultanhisar, Nysa, Nazilli/Kestel, Büyük Menderes corridor, Cayi/Eski Çine, and adjacent frontier zones
principles: Do not back-project later Ottoman administrative boundaries into 1326.
Political control, settlement continuity, route significance, and economic activity are separate evidence dimensions.
A later monument or administrative record is not by itself proof of a 1326 political boundary.
Where Aydinid, Menteshe, and Germiyan frontiers converge, preserve uncertainty rather than drawing a synthetic polygon.

anchors.name: Sultanhisar / Nysa
anchors.control: Aydinid-associated after the 1308 conquest of Aydin-ili; exact 1326 local boundary not independently resolved

anchors.name: Aydin / Tralles-Guzelhisar
anchors.control: Aydinid after Mehmed Bey's conquest around 1309; exact 1326 urban extent unresolved

anchors.name: Nazilli / Kestel region
anchors.control: frontier zone; do not assign a precise 1326 polity polygon

anchors.name: Eski Çine
anchors.control: Menteshe-associated cultural and political center by the early 14th century; exact 1326 boundary relative to Aydinid territory remains unresolved

anchors.name: Çine / northern Menteshe gateway
anchors.control: Menteshe-associated; model as a gateway toward the Büyük Menderes basin rather than as a modern district polygon

regional_findings: TDV places Aydinid territory from the Büyük Menderes through Tire, Ayasuluk and Birgi and records Mehmed Bey's conquest of Sultanhisar among the early expansions.
Aydin/Tralles lies on the northern edge of the Büyük Menderes valley and became an important Aydinid center after the conquest around 1309.

The Nazilli plain is a major natural junction: the Büyük Menderes corridor connects the Aegean coast with the interior, while northern valleys lead toward Lydia and the Harpasos/Akçay corridor leads toward Caria.

The Kestel evidence is particularly useful as a negative control: modern scholarship explicitly places the area near the interacting Aydinid, Germiyanid and Menteshe frontiers, so a smooth single-polity boundary would overstate certainty.

Eski Çine is associated with Menteshe political and cultural activity in the early fourteenth century and should be treated as a Menteshe-side anchor while keeping the exact 7 April 1326 boundary unresolved.
The Büyük Menderes basin should be represented as a physical and economic corridor independently of political ownership.
runtimeImplications: Create a frontier-band representation between Aydinid, Menteshe and Germiyan evidence rather than forcing a hard border where sources do not support one.
Represent Nazilli as a route-junction/economic node even if its 1326 political owner remains unresolved.
Represent Büyük Menderes and Harpasos/Akçay as route and terrain constraints used by the simulation.
Keep later Ottoman sanjak/kaza boundaries out of canonical 1326 geometry generation.
